claims.text: TC4 has a typical dual-phase alpha-plus-beta microstructure.
The typical alpha-plus-beta microstructure of TC4 provides favorable strength and ductility.
Untreated TC4 has low hardness and poor friction and wear properties under extreme contact stresses.
The proposed intervention deposits a (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 nanoflake coating on TC4 using spray-assisted laser cladding.
Optimizing laser power, scan speed, atmosphere, preheating, and cooling can preserve or form the desired 2D nanoflake morphology during laser cladding.
Low-thermal-input laser processing can produce strong adhesion while avoiding detrimental thermal alteration of TC4.
The coating will form an interconnected, robust, self-adaptive network of 2D HEA nanoflakes that is efficiently bonded to TC4.
(MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 nanoflakes facilitate shear-induced energy dissipation during sliding.
(MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 nanoflakes exhibit stress-induced tribocatalytic activity at high contact pressures.
The tribocatalytic activity can form a lubricious amorphous-carbon tribolayer using residual ethanol as a carbon source.
Ambient moisture may aid formation of the proposed lubricious amorphous film.
The in situ lubricious film and nanoflake deformation reduce friction and wear.

A conventionally air-sprayed (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 coating achieved an average coefficient of friction of about 0.076 and a wear rate of about 2.6 x 10^-9 mm3/(N m) on a steel-against-steel tribopair at 0.936 GPa in ambient conditions.
Applying the same lubricant through laser cladding on TC4 will significantly reduce coefficient of friction and wear rate relative to untreated TC4 under high contact load.
The coated TC4 will retain the substrate's intrinsic mechanical stability and beneficial properties.
The proposed coating is expected to remain effective at contact pressures around 0.936 GPa in ambient environments.
Departures from the optimized laser-processing window may compromise coating integrity or TC4 substrate properties.
